newsitem.title: USA: SIA concerned about bank bill's muni provision.
newsitem.headline: SIA concerned about bank bill's muni provision.

text.p: The Securities Industry Association told a key U.S. House chairman Tuesday it has concerns about a U.S. bank bill provision that would let banks directly underwrite municipal revenue bonds.

"If the purpose of financial services legislation is to restructure the regulatory scheme while reducing risk to the taxpayer, then any new securities activity should take place in a separately regulated entity, not in the bank itself," SIA President Marc Lackritz said.
Lackritz outlined his concerns in a three-page letter to Sen. Thomas Bliley, R-Va., chairman of the House Commerce Committee.

The Bliley committee's subpanel on finance, chaired by Rep. Michael Oxley, R-Ohio, is set to take testimony Wednesday from securities and banking industry CEOs on H.R. 10, which would overhaul antiquated U.S. financial laws.
Lackritz noted that current law bars banks from underwriting most municipal revenue bonds in the bank. All such underwriting must be conducted in a separate broker-dealer affiliate.

"Ironically, H.R. 10 actually expands the permissible securities activities that banks can engage in directly in the bank to include underwriting and dealing in municipal revenue bonds," Lackritz said.
Lackritz may not have long to worry about the muni provision. Industry lobbyists say that it is likely to be dropped from the bill shortly.
